extracted.intended_audience: 17th-century natural philosophers, anatomists, physicians, and astronomers (readers of the Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for reporting anatomical dissections, embryological descriptions, telescope design and testing, and astronomical observations (Jupiter spots, comets) as exemplified in 17th-century natural-philosophy reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of anatomical illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing can be more unnatural than the figure given in the plate belonging to these observations, of the uterus and its appendages. By 'testiculi' are meant the ovaria, and what are termed vasa deferentia ... the shape, situation and direction of the Fallopian tubes are strangely misrepresented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should faithfully represent anatomical shape, situation and direction; mislabelling (e.g., calling ovaria 'testiculi') or distorted depictions are misleading. If compelled to reproduce originals, note their inaccuracies and state the main valid purpose (e.g., to show oviform vesicles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vesicle (egg) conditions and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The vesicles or eggs in all sorts of females are to be considered in three conditions: 1. When they are fastened to the place where nature has lodged them as in a repository. 2. When they are loosened from thence. 3. When they enclose the embryo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on 'eggs' or vesicles, explicitly distinguish which condition is observed; provide dissection evidence for attachment/looseness and for whether the vesicle contains an embryo. Cite comparative anatomy and prior authors when classifying observed vesicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence linking vesicles to conception
rubrics_metrics.description: After conception, that which encloses the foetus is almost like an egg; amnios and chorion are always found enwrapping the child; a yellow substance (corpus luteum) is found where oviform vesicles were ruptured and cicatrices on the ovaria's surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence of amnios and chorion, corpus luteum, and ovarian surface scars as anatomical evidence that vesicles relate to conception. But note that many physiological explanations remain conjectural and should be presented cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority comparison and caution about conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: It is obvious that these explanations of physiologists are for the most part conjectural ... This is irreconcilable with the observations of Haller and other accurate physiologists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare new observations against established authorities (Fallopius, Harvey, Hippocrates, Aristotle, Haller, etc.). Highlight where observations conflict with prior 'accurate' physiologists and mark conjectural explanations as tentative. Do not overclaim from single or poorly supported dissections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embryo staging by morphological features
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of embryos at various ages: 3–4 days a little mass with head beginning to be distinguished; 14–15 days face and principal parts beginning to appear; three weeks cartilages present; one month whole human shape; six weeks bones observable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dating embryos, report the specific morphological markers (head/body distinction, eyes/nose/mouth/ears, cartilages vs bones, jawbone composition). Also state methods of dating and include caveats: miscarried/aborted embryos may have been retained or malnourished and thus be smaller than typical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for variability in embryo/egg size
rubrics_metrics.description: Those eggs are of different sizes ... embryos which miscarry have often remained a long while in the body before they came forth, or have lived there so sickly, as not to draw perhaps half the nourishment necessary for them, and therefore much less than they otherwise would be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume strict proportionality between embryonic size and time across all specimens; consider nutritional status, retention time, species differences, and stage variation when interpreting size. Use comparative samples where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative reasoning for egg size across species
rubrics_metrics.description: The reason why the eggs of fowls are always proportionably greater than those of women and of quadrupeds is, that they, when laid, must contain the matter not only for forming, but also for feeding the young animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use functional and life-history reasoning (e.g., whether egg must contain nourishment after laying) to explain interspecies egg-size differences; provide analogies (seeds → plants) and avoid assuming adult size dictates seed/egg size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telescope scaling: aperture and charge versus length
rubrics_metrics.description: Table: for various telescope lengths (feet) the proportions of apertures and proportions of the charges (diameter of spheres on which eye-glass convex surfaces are to be ground) are given; examples show how to scale aperture and magnification from a known short tube to longer tubes by proportionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing reflecting telescopes, use proportional relationships between tube length (semidiameter of grinding sphere), aperture, and eye-glass charge to predict analogous performance at other lengths. Always verify theoretical scaling by experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telescope distinctness testing (reading distance and aperture obstruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare two telescopes by reading at the distance of between 100 and 120 feet; an obstacle of a given breadth is requisite to intercept all the light which came from one point of the object, determining the effective aperture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test distinctness by practical reading-distance trials (e.g., 100–120 ft) and by using aperture obstruction to determine the required aperture that isolates light from a single point. Report exact testing conditions and measured apertures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflectivity trade-offs: metal mirrors versus glass optics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metal reflects less light than glass transmits; remedy by assigning a shallower charge in proportion to the aperture. Some metalline substances polish and reflect better and tarnish less; preservation methods (keep dry, immerse in spirit of wine) and recovery (rubbing with soft leather) recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on or designing reflecting instruments, quantify and discuss losses due to reflection vs transmission. Adjust optical geometry (shallower charge) to compensate; describe polishing and preservation techniques, and note metal selection and maintenance to minimize tarnish and loss of reflectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction guidance for metal mirrors (width, thickness, edge figure)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a four-foot tube, since the aperture should be 5 or 6 inches, there will be required a piece of metal 7 or 8 inches broad at least, because the figure will scarcely be true to the edges. The thickness of the metal must be proportional to the breadth, lest it bend in the grinding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify raw material dimensions (breadth, thickness) proportional to intended aperture to avoid deformation during grinding; note edge-figure problems and recommend testing with multiple eye-glasses to select best charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and observational criteria for Jupiter spots
rubrics_metrics.description: Two sorts of spots on Jupiter: (1) shadows of the four satellites — precisely found where some satellite is seen by the sun, moving from east to west with motion equal to that of the satellite; (2) spots independent of satellites — resemble solar spots or lunar features, motion unequal (swifter near centre), narrow near circumference, likely superficial and adhered to belts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate spot types by checking dependence on satellite position, motion regularity and equality to satellite motion, changes with parallax and opposition, and by analyzing apparent motion across disk (central speed vs edge). Describe attachment to belts and typical sizes relative to planet diameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring planetary rotation/revolution periods and precision corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of the permanent spot's apparent revolution found to be nine hours and 55–56 minutes by many observations; for greater exactness, add ordinary equation of days and particular equation depending on Jupiter's motion inequality; use repeated observations and account for leap years in cumulative counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine rotation/revolution periods via repeated observations and cumulative counts; apply corrections for the equation of days and planet motion inequalities to improve precision. Report epoch and predicted future return times; discuss observational limitations (horizon time, weather).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using regular planetary features for longitude determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This revolution being the swiftest and the most regular that is hitherto known in the Heavens, a traveller alone, even without having any correspondence with other observers, may make use of it to find the longitudes of the most remote places of the earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a planetary feature has a well-determined period and predictable returns, it can be used as a time-reference for finding longitude. Provide period, epoch, and tables or procedures to compute expected return times at different dates; note precision limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comet observational description and positional measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a telescope the comet appeared as a star of the third magnitude. With a 17-foot telescope the head appeared almost round and well defined, distinguished from the mistiness (chevelure). The tail was seen turned opposite to the sun; whole comet occupied three or four minutes of a degree; position was given by line with known stars and mapped to ecliptic coordinates (23°25' Taurus, lat. 14° N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe comet morphology (head, chevelure, tail), note tail direction relative to sun, estimate naked-eye magnitude and telescopic details, measure angular size in minutes of degree, and determine position by alignment with known stars; transfer observed place to star maps to give celestial coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book review inclusion criteria: novelty and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Hodges's treatise on the plague ... is so well known to medical men, that it would be superfluous to retain the analysis given by Mr. Oldenburg of its contents. ... 'Contains nothing worth notice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing books, judge whether the contents offer novel or useful information to the intended readership; omit detailed analysis of well-known works or works that 'contain nothing worth notice.' Indicate if a work is incorporated into a larger reference (and so need not be separately detailed).
